motions.title: Update on Policy Review Program
motions.description: Quarterly status update on the 2024 Policy Review Program and revised completion timeframes for Financial Reserves and Endowment Lands Account, Risk Management, and State Administrative Tribunal Policies.

motions.title: Rescind Accounting Standards Policy
motions.description: Rescission of the Accounting Standards Policy adopted in August 1995. The policy is no longer necessary as compliance with Australian Accounting Standards is mandated through the Local Government Act 1995 and Local Government (Financial Management) Regulations 1996, and the policy creates risk of conflict with current standards and annual financial statements.

motions.title: Revocation of Council Policy 070 – Public Liability Insurance
motions.description: Council Policy 070 seeks to ensure that all hirers using the Town's sports grounds, reserves and community facilities have adequate Public Liability Insurance. The requirement for public liability has been incorporated into the conditions of hire for both community facilities and open spaces, making the standalone policy redundant.

motions.title: Review of Vehicle Crossover Policy - Administration Recommendation
motions.description: The Vehicle Crossover Policy has been amended to improve clarity and consistency in relation to the design, construction, and approval of vehicle crossovers within the Town. Key amendments include clarification of permitted crossover widths, specification of approved materials and colours, inclusion of provisions for commercial and temporary crossovers, introduction of approval validity periods, streamlined guidance on verge tree clearance requirements, and updated references to related standards and documents.

motions.title: Amendment to Vehicle Crossover Policy - Town-Initiated Works
motions.description: Amendment to add a new Section 21 addressing Town-Initiated Works Affecting Existing Vehicle Crossovers. The amendment specifies that where the Town undertakes renewal or upgrade works to Town-owned rights-of-way affecting existing bitumen vehicle crossovers, the Town will ordinarily replace the affected crossover with a concrete vehicle crossover constructed in accordance with the specifications, subject to circumstances where replacement would be inappropriate or impractical.

motions.title: Vehicle Crossover Policy - Substantive Motion (as amended)
motions.description: The substantive motion on the amended Vehicle Crossover Policy, incorporating the amendment adding Section 21 on Town-Initiated Works Affecting Existing Vehicle Crossovers.

motions.title: Legislative, Policy and Case Law Update – Local Government Sector
motions.description: Update on recent legislative reforms to the Local Government Act 1995, establishment of Local Government Inspector and Panel of Monitors, amendments to local law review requirements, court proceedings affecting elected members, and the State Development Act 2025.

motions.title: Review of Complaints and Unreasonable Behaviour Management Policy
motions.description: Review of Complaints and Unreasonable Behaviour Management Policy to ensure consistent, transparent and effective complaint handling, with proposed amendments to clarify scope and strengthen governance.

motions.title: Complaints and Unreasonable Behaviour Management Policy
motions.description: Review and adoption of amended Complaints and Unreasonable Behaviour Management Policy, which clarifies scope, strengthens governance arrangements, and establishes a clearer framework for complaint management. The policy was first adopted in 2004 and has been subject to periodic review. In September 2024, Council endorsed a revised approach whereby the Policy was retained as a high-level framework and operational detail was moved to supporting guidelines.

motions.title: Council Logo Policy
motions.description: Review and revision of the Council Logo Policy to simplify requirements for permitted use of the Town of Cambridge logo and align with the official Town of Cambridge Brand Style Guide endorsed by Council in April 2024.

motions.title: Review of Elected Member Entitlements Policy
motions.description: Review and adoption of amended Elected Member and Independent Committee Member Entitlements Policy. Recent reforms to the Local Government Act 1995 and associated regulations have strengthened the role and independence of ARICs. The Salaries and Allowances Tribunal issued amendments introducing specific provisions for sitting fees and reimbursement of expenses for Independent Members of ARICs.

The motion was amended to reduce the budget allocation from $30,000 to $4,000.

The committee comprises six elected members and the CEO (non-voting). Terms of reference were adopted and an amendment was made to remove 'Policies and Strategy' from the Community and Resources Committee terms of reference.

motions.title: Light Vehicle Replacement Program
motions.description: Council approved the acquisition and disposal of 18 light fleet vehicles identified for replacement in the 2021/2022 financial year, including seven Sport Utility Vehicles (SUVs) and 11 utility vehicles. The proposal includes fleet standardisation to the Toyota RAV4 GX Hybrid for SUVs and standardisation of utility vehicles to one make where possible, with estimated acquisition costs of $608,100, trade-in value of $446,500, and net changeover cost of $161,600.

motions.title: Energy Sustainability and Renewables Project
motions.description: Council approved participation in the WA Local Government Sustainable Energy Future Tender for the development of a Local Government Power Purchase Agreement allowing for the adoption of 100% renewable energy at contestable sites for a three year contract term commencing April 2022. The Town will purchase renewable energy from three accredited windfarms (Emu Downs, Collar and Albany) with an additional annual cost of $81,244 for 100% renewable uptake.

motions.title: Jubilee Park – Basketball Half-Court
motions.description: Council approved the concept design for a basketball half-court facility and ancillary items at Jubilee Park, City Beach. The project responds to a petition received in February 2019 with 16 signatures requesting installation of a half-court basketball facility. The facility will be 12 metres long by 16 metres wide with a Plexipave surface, limestone block wall behind the hoop for seating and ball barrier, new pathway and pram ramp from Challenger Parade, and limestone block edging to replace existing log edge.

motions.title: Marlow Street, Cambridge to Ruislip Street, Wembley Road Modifications – Final Consultation Outcomes
motions.description: Council considered the outcomes of community consultation relating to the removal of five centre island Angophora costata street trees on Marlow Street, Wembley and the planting of 11 verge Lophostemon confertus trees. The consultation showed 70% of respondents supported the removal of the centre island trees (74% when considering household responses). The removal addresses damage to the road caused by tree root systems. Additional funding of $60,000 from the Durston Road resurfacing project variance is required, with total removal and remedial works cost of $159,116.

motions.description: Seeking Council approval in principle of Draft 2021-2022 Budget prior to advertising for public comment for one week (28 July - 4 August 2021). Budget establishes 0% increase in Gross Rental Value rate generating $26.1M in rates, fifth consecutive year of 0% increase due to COVID-19 recovery. Total operating revenue $53M, total operating expenditure $60.7M, capital works $23.8M. Proposes amendment to Area Improvement Reserve Fund purpose to include funding for Mindarie Regional Council operational changes ($7.1M payout).

motions.title: Australian Masters Games Sponsorship Request – Decline

Games comprise 40-55 sports, approximately 8,000 expected participants plus volunteers and spectators, with approximately 60% travelling from outside host state. Sponsorship not recommended due to minimal expected economic impact, limited Town capacity to leverage benefits, and COVID-19 risk.

Overall state of IT system is in initial/ad hoc (unsatisfactory) state requiring significant resources over at least 5 years.

motions.title: Occupational Safety and Health Legislation Update – Reception and Note

Work Health and Safety Bill 2019 passed 3 November 2020, received royal assent 10 November 2020, anticipated to come into effect mid-2021 when regulations finalised. Report covers duty of care, duty to workers, consultation requirements, officers' due diligence duty, penalties, industrial manslaughter offences, psychological health duties, inspector powers, and implications for Town employees.

motions.description: A procedural motion was moved to defer the Complaints Management Policy and Code of Conduct review to an Elected Member Forum for consideration of different models.

motions.title: Adopt Complaints Management Policy and Code of Conduct
motions.description: Council approved by absolute majority the adoption of the revised Complaints Management Policy and Code of Conduct, following amendments to address complaint investigation responsibilities, bullying provisions, and procedures for handling complaints and allegations.

motions.title: Adopt Compliance, Prosecution and Enforcement Policy
motions.description: Council approved by absolute majority the revised Compliance, Prosecution and Enforcement Policy following a Notice of Motion requesting improvements to Show Cause letter issuance processes. The policy amendments clarify procedures for obtaining CEO consent before issuing Show Cause letters and define enforcement procedures.

motions.title: Receive Information Bulletin September 2020
motions.description: Council received the Information Bulletin dated September 2020, which provides information to the Community and Elected Members regarding ongoing matters including SAT appeals, MetroWest development applications, petitions, notices of motion, and other administrative matters.

motions.title: Request CEO report on streetlight poles ownership
motions.description: Mayor Shannon moved a Notice of Motion requesting the CEO provide an update report regarding the Town's ability to retain ownership of streetlight poles installed as part of the Floreat and Wembley undergrounding project. The motion notes Western Power's refusal in 2018 and identifies benefits of ownership including reduced energy costs through tendering and potential smart lighting implementation.

motions.title: Approve Summer Clipper Bus Service for 2020/21
motions.description: Council approved by absolute majority a Notice of Motion to reallocate $47,715 for the Summer Clipper Bus Service to operate from 4 December 2020 to 31 January 2021 using the Town's own community buses with hired drivers, following the same route as 2018-19 operations.

motions.title: Request procedure for SAT matters contrary to administration recommendation
motions.description: A Notice of Motion requested the CEO prepare a report formalising a procedure for State Administrative Tribunal matters arising from council decisions contrary to administration recommendations, including provisions for council briefing notes, alternate officer coordination, and elected member attendance at mediations.

motions.title: Request records management review
motions.description: A Notice of Motion requested the CEO undertake a review of record keeping and management of the Town to ensure compliance with record management policies, the State Records Act 2000, the Developer Contact With Planning Staff Policy, and Office of the Auditor General recommendations. The amended motion was redirected to the Audit Committee with reporting deadline of February 2021.

motions.title: Approve CEO delegation for SUB.CO submarine cable agreements
motions.description: Council approved by absolute majority delegated authority to the CEO to sign a Non-Disclosure Agreement with SUB.CO and execute a Deed of Settlement for installation of a submarine cable terminus and manhole at Fred Burton Car Park, City Beach, for the Oman-Perth submarine communications cable project.

motions.title: Alderbury Sports Ground Change Room and Toilet Facilities
motions.description: Council considered the concept design for proposed new change room and toilet facilities at Alderbury Sports Ground. The Mayor circulated a briefing note from Council to the CEO requesting design improvements including reducing change rooms from 4 to 2, deleting lockers, increasing public toilets, and improving the façade.

motions.title: Lake Monger Area 4 – Pump/Jump Track Consultation Outcomes
motions.description: Council considered the community consultation feedback for the proposed pump/jump track at Lake Monger Area 4. The consultation showed over 80% support for the proposal. Council was asked to approve the revised Lake Monger Activity Plan 2020 and creation of a project working group with potential users to develop a design brief.

motions.title: Town of Cambridge – Proposed Verge Valet Bulk Waste Collection Service
motions.description: Council considered implementing a trial Verge Valet bulk waste collection service between 1 November 2020 and 30 June 2022. The service aims to reduce waste disposal costs and provide a personalised service to residents through bookable collections rather than zone-based collection.

motions.title: Quarry Amphitheatre – Volunteer Ushers
motions.description: Council considered the engagement and management of volunteer ushers for the Quarry Amphitheatre. Issues included occupational health and safety concerns, fire management practices, and insurance risk advice. An initial motion to approve the Administration Recommendation was lost, followed by an amended motion addressing fire risk assessment.

motions.title: Quarry Amphitheatre Fees and Charges
motions.description: Council considered assistance for hirers of the Quarry Amphitheatre whilst Western Australia remains in Phase 4 of COVID-19 restrictions. A 50% reduction in venue hire charges was proposed to offset reduced audience capacity from gathering restrictions.

motions.title: Bold Park Aquatic – 2020 Royal Life Saving Society WA Safety Audit
motions.description: Council received the results of the 2020 water safety assessment conducted by Royal Life Saving Society WA at Bold Park Aquatic, which was completed on 25 June 2020. The facility achieved a safety score of 98.87% with only minor recommendations for improvement.

motions.title: Reabold Tennis Club Liquor Licence Extension

motions.title: Tender 2020-11 Herdsman to Perry Lakes Drainage Diversion

Two submissions were received from Resolute Australia Civil Contractors Pty Ltd and Civcon Civil & Project Management Pty Ltd, evaluated against criteria including relevant experience, key personnel skills, capacity/resources, demonstrated understanding, environmental factor, and price.

motions.title: Memorials in Public Places Policy
motions.description: Rescind existing Policy 5.2.2 Footpaths – Laying of Memorial Plaques and adopt new comprehensive policy for memorials in public places. The new policy addresses requests for personal memorials including park benches with commemorative plaques, memorial trees, roadside crosses, shelters, and spreading of ashes. Proposed amendments to Fees and Charges for memorial installations.

motions.title: Western Metropolitan Regional Council MoU Annual Contribution
motions.description: Authorization for Chief Executive Officer to sign a Memorandum of Understanding between the Town of Cambridge and the Western Metropolitan Regional Council (WMRC) for the provision of resource recovery services. WMRC restricted free access to their transfer station in Shenton Park and proposed the Town contribute to operational costs so Cambridge residents can continue accessing household hazardous waste, recycling and problematic waste services.

motions.title: Community Events Program 2020/2021
motions.description: Approval of proposed Town of Cambridge Festivals and Events program for 2020/2021 financial year, modified due to COVID-19 restrictions to focus on small, localized events. Program includes playground activations, music in the park series, Australia Day celebration, Christmas light trail, festival of lights and sounds, ANZAC day celebrations, and community awards function. Discussion regarding number and scale of events evolved, with final recommendation to approve Lake Monger Christmas Tree Lights and defer other events pending COVID-19 directions.

motions.title: Resolution to Prepare New Local Planning Scheme and Endorse Outline Project Plan
motions.description: Council resolution to formally commence the preparation of Local Planning Scheme No. 2, endorse an outline project plan for the preparation, and delegate authority to the Development Committee to endorse 'guiding principles' during the preparation process. motions.title: Nanson Street traffic management treatment
motions.description: Council decision on petition received 12 November 2019 requesting traffic management treatment (speed humps) on Nanson Street between Grantham Street and Scaddan Street, Wembley. Community consultation resulted in 19 responses (47% support, 53% opposition). Traffic assessment indicates treatment not justified.

motions.title: Marlow Street parking restrictions
motions.description: Council decision on proposed parking restrictions on Marlow Street between Grantham Street and Herdsman Parade, Wembley. Community engagement survey of 36 residents yielded 21 responses with Option 3 (no parking both sides with resident permits) preferred at 48%. Decision deferred pending Parking Strategic Working Group review of Residential Parking Permits.

motions.title: City Beach lighting upgrade
motions.description: Council approval of design for upgrading lighting in City Beach coastal precinct to meet Australian Standards AS1158. Project includes LED technology upgrade to iconic mast tower lighting (40% more energy efficient) and enhanced lighting to pedestrian pathways and carparks. Estimated cost $405,000.

motions.title: Dunblane Park concept design approval
motions.description: Proposed upgrade to Dunblane Park, Floreat to address poor amenity and decline of turfed areas. Design includes kerb extension into Moray Avenue to narrow road for traffic calming, replacement of scheme water reticulation with connection to Lothian Park bore (242m underground boring), new pathway, seating, and tree plantings. Committee supported more economical design with less ecozoning. Procedural motion deferred for one month to prepare two options with revised costings.

motions.title: Ocean Village Park lighting replacement
motions.description: Council approval of design for replacement lighting at Ocean Village Park, City Beach to meet Australian Standards AS1158.3.1. Existing lighting from 1996 insufficient and end of useful life. LED design reduces spill light to residences, enhances visual character. Approximately 140 metres of previously unlit pathway to be lit. Estimated cost $210,000.

motions.title: Oban Road Parking and Landscaping Improvements Endorsement

The partnership includes initiatives for training, safe assessments, defibrillators, event health services, and community transport services. An indicative budget of $35,000 for 2018/2019 is proposed with $18,000 in additional funds required.

motions.title: Bold Park Aquatic Centre Fees and Charges 2018/2019
motions.description: Review of current fees and charges for entry, programs and services at Bold Park Aquatic Centre. The report recommends minor increases to entry and program fees of approximately 1.5% to reflect current market prices and increases in utilities and other costs. No increases proposed for Swim School enrolments or Centre Memberships due to competition from Scarborough Beach Pool.

motions.title: Age Friendly Community Plan and Seniors Services Strategy
motions.description: Creating Communities completed an Age-Friendly Community Plan (AFCP) with recommendations confirming that senior residents want to age-in-place. A Cambridge Seniors Services Strategy for 2018/19-2021/22 is proposed to establish a small Senior Services team to support older people (55+). Total funding of $255,000 operational and $12,000 capital requested for 2018/19.

motions.title: Challenger Parade Pedestrian Improvements and Traffic Calming Measures
motions.description: The Town received 175 responses to a community survey seeking views on proposed options to improve pedestrian crossings and traffic calming measures on Challenger Parade near the Surf Club Building and Commercial Development at City Beach. Options included permanent staff with 75% Sunday loading and casual staff with 75% loading plus 25% casual loading, with estimated annual costs between $60,000 and $100,000.

motions.title: Cost of Study Area at Boulevard Centre Oceanic Room
motions.description: Report on the cost of providing a study area at the Boulevard Centre (Oceanic Room) for Cambridge Library customers. Three options presented: casual use at no cost during peak times, exclusive use for 52 weeks at $31,000 per annum, or exclusive use during peak times at $11,000 per annum.

motions.title: Policy Review - Community Funding Programs
motions.description: Review of Council Policy 2.1.15 - Community Funding Programs. Recommendation to simplify and consolidate funding programs from seven to four programs: Youth Achievement Grant, Facilities Grant, Community Organisations Support Grant, and Community Development Grant (with three funding levels). Changes effective from 1 July 2018.

motions.title: Policy Review - Community Development Directorate
motions.description: Review of Council policies pertaining to Community Development Directorate covering Community Development, Library Services, and Wembley Golf Course. Policies to be retained unchanged, amended, or deleted as detailed. Notable changes include updates to reflect Locals First Approach and minor amendments to various policies.

motions.title: Underground Power: LED Street Lights Roll Out
motions.description: Report on achieving 100% LED street lighting and smart controller compatibility in SUPP and Wembley/West Leederville underground power projects. Four options presented: retrofit existing installations, defer street lighting works, delay projects by 6 months, or do nothing. Administration recommended Option 1 (retrofit) as lowest cost and time impact approach.

motions.description: Receipt of report on items considered at Mindarie Regional Council meetings on 1 September 2016 and 20 October 2016.

motions.title: Waste Local Law 2016 - Adoption
motions.description: To adopt the proposed Town of Cambridge Waste Local Law 2016 following public consultation. No submissions received from the general public during the consultation period closing 1 July 2016.

motions.title: Local Government and Public Property Local Law 2016 - Adoption
motions.description: To adopt the proposed Town of Cambridge Local Government and Public Property Local Law 2016, which will replace the law adopted on 24 April 2001. No submissions received from the general public during the consultation period closing 14 September 2016.

motions.title: Cambridge Bowling Club Five-A-Side Soccer - Sub-lease Approval
motions.description: To approve the Cambridge Bowling Club's sub-lease to Fox Football Fives Pty Ltd for a Five-A-Side soccer facility. Community consultation received 4 responses; all supported the competition but 2 residents requested reduced hours. Hours amended from 9.30am to 10.15pm to 9.30am to 9.30pm following consultation feedback.

motions.title: Expression of Interest 47-16 - Children's Theatre at Quarry Amphitheatre - Result Noted
motions.description: EOI process for provision of a children's theatre at the Quarry Amphitheatre (8 October to 31 October 2016) resulted in no written submissions. Constraints include limited venue availability and lack of heating.

motions.title: West City Church Nanson Street Christmas Party - Approval
motions.description: To approve the 2016 West City Church of Christ Nanson Street Christmas Party event on Sunday 18 December 2016. Expected attendance of approximately 2,000 people requiring Category 2 event status and council approval.

motions.title: Bold Park Aquatic - Small Pool Inflatable Hire Fee
motions.description: To adopt a new fee of $75 (ex GST) per hour for exclusive use of the small pool inflatable (suitable for ages 5-7 years) at Bold Park Aquatic Centre, effective from 5 December 2016. Requires statutory advertising under Local Government Act 1995 section 6.19.

motions.title: Bold Park Aquatic - Heating Study
motions.description: To approve unbudgeted expenditure of $50,000 for a scoping study into pool heating options at Bold Park Aquatic. Three existing 200 kW electric heat pumps are reaching end of service life. Study to be completed by end March 2017 to guide budget allocation in FY18 for construction works in summer 2017/2018.

motions.title: South City Beach Kiosk & Toilets - Future Use and Demolition
motions.description: To approve funding for demolition of the old South City Beach Kiosk and Toilet building following engineering assessment showing significant damage ($40,000), heritage recording ($5,000), and community consultation prior to demolition.

motions.title: Lake Monger Activity Plan - Community Engagement
motions.description: To endorse the draft Lake Monger Activity Plan for community engagement and approve the proposed engagement process. Community workshop held 29 June 2016 with approximately 30 participants. Elected member workshop held 5 October 2016. Consultation period proposed to extend through February 2017.

motions.title: Documents Sealed - 22 November 2016
motions.description: To note that documents have been affixed with the Common Seal of the Town of Cambridge. Three documents listed: Professional Golfers Association Lease (25 Oct 2016), Kidsafe WA Public Art Notification (25 Oct 2016), and Mindarie Regional Council Deed of Variation (8 Nov 2016).

motions.title: Payment of Accounts - October 2016
motions.description: Confirmation of schedule of accounts for October 2016 as required by Regulation 13 of the Local Government (Financial Management) Regulations 1996.

motions.title: Investment Schedule - October 2016
motions.description: Receipt of Investment Schedule as at 31 October 2016 showing investment portfolio performance and distribution across various financial institutions.

motions.title: Monthly Financial Statements, Review and Variances - October 2016
motions.description: Review of financial position for period ended 31 October 2016 including permanent and timing variances. Included capital works reallocations for South City Beach Toodyay Retaining Wall repairs and Perry Lakes South toilet block refurbishment.

motions.title: Second Storey Addition - West Leederville Primary School
motions.description: Application for second storey addition to library building for five new classrooms and staff room at West Leederville Primary School, Lot 302 (No. 58) Northwood Street, West Leederville. Referral from Department of Finance, Building Management and Works. Committee amendment added requirement for full contribution from Department of Education for parking and road network improvements.

motions.title: Chinese Massage and Consulting Room - Wembley
motions.description: Application for Chinese Massage and consulting room for acupuncture and cupping at Lot 2 (No. 228A) Cambridge Street, Wembley. Committee amended approval to acupuncture and cupping only, excluding massage, with 6-month approval period. Applicant certified as registered Chinese Medicine Practitioner with general registration as acupuncturist.

motions.title: Home occupation (health coach) approval
motions.description: Application for home occupation (health coach) submitted by Rachelle Teune at Lot 59 (No. 35) Evandale Street, Floreat. Applicant proposed reducing sessions from 9 to 6 hours per week with options for client parking, carpooling, and client number reduction.

motions.title: Home Occupation - Health Coach - Referred Back
motions.description: Application for home occupation (health coach) at Lot 59 (No. 35) Evandale Street, Floreat, referred back from 25 October 2016 council meeting for consideration of reducing client numbers. Application involves fitness and nutrition coaching from front garage with multiple clients.

motions.title: Three storey dwelling approval
motions.description: Application for a three storey dwelling at Lot 280 (No. 9) Callington Avenue, City Beach. Dwelling has multiple levels, flat roof, extensive glazing, rendered walls and cladding. Lower floor partly cut into site, garage not visible from street, top floor set well back. Applicant Karl Spargo Building Design. Multiple amended plans submitted to address design principles and neighbour concerns regarding building setbacks.

motions.title: Roofed deck application refused
motions.description: Application to construct a roof over previously approved open roof deck of two storey dwelling under construction at Lot 334 (No. 110) Branksome Gardens, City Beach. Original approval from 23 September 2014 with condition that no roof or cover be placed over roof deck. Proposal includes roof and window enclosure creating height variation and adverse impact on amenity of adjoining properties.

motions.title: Privacy screen and alterations approved
motions.description: Two retrospective applications for a two storey dwelling with undercroft under construction at Lot 379 (No. 40) Challenger Parade, City Beach. Applications for side boundary privacy screen (3 metre high steel frame with vertical timber slats) and modifications to upper floor privacy screening (extended to ceiling with window opening). Original approval from 23 April 2013 required privacy screen maximum 1.6 metres high with no opening.

motions.title: Two storey dwelling approved
motions.description: Application for a two storey dwelling at Lot 2 (No. 67a) St Leonards Avenue, West Leederville on rear existing survey strata lot with vehicle access from Tolano Lane. Modern design with nil setbacks at ground level to side boundaries and open space via internal courtyard. Amended plans submitted to address privacy concerns raised by adjoining property No. 65b.

motions.title: Grouped dwelling alterations approved
motions.description: Application for additions and alterations to front dwelling in strata development at Strata Lot 1 of Lot 220 (No. 433A) Cambridge Street, Floreat. Plans show new vehicular access from Cambridge Street to double carport, fencing in front setback, and rear living/dining addition. Applicant Swell Homes. Amended plans submitted to reduce boundary wall height from 4.5-5.3 metres to 3.3 metres.

motions.title: Patio application referred back
motions.description: Application for a patio at Lot 374 (No. 74) Branksome Gardens, City Beach. Plans show 7.15 metre by 2.75 metre patio setback 0.2-0.47 metres from northern boundary. Applicant Glasshouse Conservatories. Administration recommended approval subject to setback increase to minimum 0.5 metres. Committee recommendation was to refuse. Item referred back to Development Committee.

motions.title: Lot 2 Salvado Road Floreat - Fencing Condition Clearance
motions.description: Request to satisfy planning condition requiring rear boundary fence to be increased to 2.1 metres in height. Applicant proposed powder-coated aluminium slats but administration did not support this option. Motion relates to approval of the proposed metal slats with conditions.

motions.title: Lot 3 Blencowe Street West Leederville - Reconsideration of Fence Conditions
motions.description: Request for reconsideration of conditions of planning approval for front fencing. Applicant requested removal of infill panel ratio requirement and truncation condition. Motion relates to support for deleting the truncation requirement.

motions.title: Closure of Pedestrian Access Way - Perry Lakes
motions.description: Request to close Pedestrian Access Way (Lot 8008) between Lot 232 Tomlinson Boulevard and Lot 233 Stadium Drive, Floreat. Edge Visionary Living seeks to purchase the PAW for amalgamation with adjoining lots. Motion proposes advertising the closure and imposing conditions including an easement and building setback requirements.

motions.title: Local Planning Strategy - Community Engagement Strategy Endorsement
motions.description: Endorsement of the Community Engagement Strategy prepared for the Local Planning Strategy preparation. Strategy outlines three-stage engagement approach: preliminary engagement (November 2016), detailed engagement (February-March 2017), and formal advertising (mid-2018).

motions.title: Budget rate increase amendment to 2.5%
motions.description: Amendment to clause (ii)(a) to reflect an increase of no more than 2.5% overall increase on 2015/16 rates, with proposed budget savings of $573,000.

motions.title: Town Planning Scheme Amendment 31 - Legal Action Report
motions.description: Noting of report regarding ongoing Supreme Court judicial review proceedings initiated by the Coast Ward Ratepayers Association against Council's decision to adopt Town Planning Scheme Amendment 31. Total legal costs to end of June 2016 were $136,365.

motions.title: Bold Park Aquatic Centre Redevelopment - Pool Heating
motions.description: Authorization to implement supplemental heating system at Bold Park Aquatic Centre for the outdoor 50m pool. New budget of $120,000 approved to be funded from Endowment Lands Account and repaid from St John's Wood development proceeds. CEO authorized to commit single-source contract for tertiary heat pumps with installation capacity of 230 kW.

motions.title: Legal advice on JDAP extension of time for Vita development
motions.description: Request for legal advice from Moharich & Associates regarding whether the Metro West JDAP decision on 20 June 2016 to grant an extension of time to Georgiou Developments Pty Ltd was correct, specifically concerning the change to the Town's development framework for the Residential Interface Node in the West Leederville Precinct Policy.

motions.title: Bamford Lane traffic and access study
motions.description: Request for Administration to prepare a report regarding traffic and access issues in Bamford Lane associated with current and future development, considering options for the landowner ceding 1 metre of land or adjusting development controls to ensure continued rear access to properties fronting Oxford Close.

motions.title: Parking in lieu policy amendment
motions.description: Proposal to amend the parking in lieu policy to limit the 20% discount to properties within 250 metres of train stations or high-frequency bus services (every 15 minutes between 8am-6pm) and only for commercial enterprises suited to customers using public transport.

motions.title: Paved verges and traffic islands landscaping
motions.description: Request for CEO to instruct Director of Infrastructure to cease paving internal spaces on traffic islands and verges and instead plant large to medium trees interspersed with shrubs and woodchips where practicable, to improve streetscape and reduce heat island effect.

motions.title: Indian Coral tree investigation for verge planting
motions.description: Request for CEO to obtain a report from the Arbor Centre regarding the suitability of Indian Coral (Erythrina x Sykesii) trees as large canopy verge trees, specifically addressing limb failure predisposition and suitability for windy conditions.

motions.title: Temporary commercial parking permits trial
motions.description: Proposal for a three-month trial of a commercial parking permit system in areas with limited parking, allowing local businesses access to reduced-fee all-day parking in streets near their business at $10 per day, limited to 2 permits per business.

motions.title: Wembley Athletics Centre Playground - deferred/withdrawn
motions.description: Motion by Mayor Shannon to defer awarding the tender and investigate alternative sites (Perry Lakes or Lake Monger) for the playground construction, and to review design modifications to reduce maintenance costs.

motions.title: Leederville Station Pedestrian Bridge - withdrawn
motions.description: Motion by Mayor Shannon to undertake community consultation regarding amendments to the pedestrian bridge to Leederville station and surrounding area to provide access to Cambridge high street in West Leederville, and conduct a traffic assessment.

motions.title: Confirmation of Minutes 28 June 2016
motions.description: Confirmation of Minutes of the Ordinary Meeting of the Council held on 28 June 2016

motions.title: Perry Lakes Estate parking plan - circulation for comment
motions.description: Perry Lakes Estate development is at advanced stage with most lots developed. Parking pressures are evident and Town prepared parking estate plan. Proposal to circulate plan to landowners for 2 week comment period and then finalise parking plan.

motions.title: Cambridge Street parking modifications - adopt restrictions
motions.description: Urban on Cambridge development nearing completion. PTA removed bus stop on north side of Cambridge Street between Alexander and Jersey Streets. Proposal to introduce additional parking in redundant bus zone area and modify restrictions on south side following committee amendment.

motions.title: Bus shelter management program - install shelter and annual funding
motions.description: Review of options for upgrading hardstands and shelters at various bus stops. Current funding level $30,000 per year adequate for maintenance but not for increasing number of shelters. New shelters cost $10,000-$15,000 each. PTA may provide 50% funding for shelters with 15+ daily boardings.

motions.title: Blackspot funding application - Cambridge Street/McKenzie Street
motions.description: Proposal to re-submit Black Spot funding application to Main Roads WA for Cambridge Street/McKenzie Street intersection which had 5 crashes in previous 5 years. Project involves installing pedestrian refuge island with benefit cost ratio of 2.01. Local government contribution required $6,000 with project estimate $18,000.

motions.title: Treescape Plan amendment - alternate large canopy verge trees
motions.description: Council approved Notice of Motion on 24 May 2016 allowing applications for alternate verge trees not listed in Town's Treescape Plan 2010-2020. Committee agreed one species per street and included all varieties of Corymbia Ficifolia and Poinciana. Amendment approved allowing property owners to choose variety by majority vote for entire street or where street exceeds 300 metres, between major intersections.

motions.title: Mindarie Regional Council meeting items - report received
motions.description: Report on items considered at Mindarie Regional Council meeting on 7 July 2016 including 2016/17 budget adoption with members' gate fee increase from $155 to $165 per tonne (6.5% increase) and capital budget program of $16,593,900.

motions.title: MRC Constitution amendments - support proposed changes
motions.description: MRC endorsed concept of Waste Precinct and requires constitutional amendments to enable it to enter contracts for waste treatment/disposal at facilities not owned/managed/controlled by MRC or outside the region. Proposed amendment to clauses 5.1(a) and 5.1(b) to include provision for waste delivery to alternative facilities by agreement.

motions.title: 2017 Holi Festival of Colours Event - Approval
motions.description: Seeking Council support for the Indian Society of Western Australia to hold the 2017 Holi Festival of Colours event at Perry Lakes on Sunday 12 March 2017. The event was previously held at Lake Monger but 2016 attendance of approximately 5,000 people (compared to estimated 300) caused issues including inadequate parking, waste disposal, and facilities. Event is now subject to Category 2 event requirements.

motions.title: Wembley Sports Park Playground - Tender Rejection
motions.description: Motion to reject all tenders for the Wembley Sports Park Playground construction. Committee members expressed concerns regarding parking impact during netball season and requested further information on rubber softfall and maintenance costs.

motions.title: Wembley Sports Park Playground - Tender Award to Phase 3
motions.description: Following the rejection of the motion to reject all tenders, a subsequent motion to award the contract to Phase 3 Landscape Constructions for $556,025.15 plus GST for construction of the playground, picnic area and landscaping at Wembley Sports Park.

motions.title: Two storey dwelling approval - Lot 11 St Leonards Avenue
motions.description: Application for two storey dwelling at No. 122 St Leonards Avenue, West Leederville. Proposal addresses variations to front setback (upper floor encroachment of 4.75m vs 6m requirement) and vehicular access from primary street rather than right-of-way. Future subdivision layout considered in assessment. Amended plans submitted addressing roof pitch, street surveillance, visual privacy, and balcony screening.

motions.title: Lot 432 (No. 34) McKenzie Street, Wembley - Carport

motions.title: Electronic Billboard Sign - Lot 43 Cambridge Street refusal
motions.description: Application for digital screen for third party advertising on facade of building at No. 1 Cambridge Street, corner Loftus Street, West Leederville. Approximately 19 metres long and 6.5 metres high. Applicant AdBrands Media. Application assessed against Advertising Signs Policy which does not permit electronic billboard signs on private property. Proposal fails due to advertising third parties for commercial gain, dominating building, detracting from road safety, and adversely impacting streetscape and amenity. Main Roads WA advised proposal not acceptable from road safety perspective due to high crash rate, complex road alignments, location at intersection, and building height.

motions.description: Review of fees and charges for road reserves (crossover subsidies) and park reserves (access fees and bonds). Amendment passed to increase maximum Park Bond from $1,500 to $10,000.

motions.title: Cambridge Senior Services Fees and Charges 2016/2017

motions.title: Cambridge Youth Services Fees and Charges 2016/2017

motions.description: Adoption of proposed fees and charges for Quarry Amphitheatre for the 2016/2017 financial year, recommending 3% increase to most fees except for Café/Lawn area (20% reduction), abolition of security bonds, and introduction of hourly rate for radio microphones.

motions.title: Sports Grounds and Reserves Fees and Charges 2016/2017

motions.title: Sports Grounds and Reserves Fees - Amendment (CPI Only)
motions.description: Foreshadowed amendment to CR16.78 proposing that fee increases be limited to 1.5% (current CPI) rather than 3%. Amendment moved during Committee Meeting 16 May 2016.

motions.title: Sports Grounds and Reserves Fees - Second Amendment (CPI Only)
motions.description: Second amendment during Council debate proposing that fee increases be limited to 1.5% (current CPI). Amendment lost 3/6.

motions.title: Boulevard Centre Fees and Charges 2016/2017
motions.description: Adoption of proposed fees and charges for The Boulevard Centre for the 2016/2017 financial year. Due to declining revenue from reduced government training funding, it is recommended to reduce venue hire fees to remain competitive with new competing facilities.

motions.title: Wembley Community Centre and Leederville Town Hall Fees 2016/2017
motions.description: Adoption of proposed fees and charges for Wembley Community Centre and Leederville Town Hall for the 2016/2017 financial year, recommending 3% increase to room hire fees with rounding.

motions.description: Design and construction of bin store for Odyssea Beach Cafe (Tenancy B), public notice of disposition, lease deed variation, and unbudgeted expenditure approval from Endowment Lands Account

motions.title: Change of use to Small Bar - Gayton Road
motions.description: Application for change of use to 'small bar' at Lot 800 and Lot 12 (No. 31) Gayton Road, City Beach. The tenancy has existing approval for 'restaurant' use; applicant seeks additional approval for 'small bar' use. Five submissions received expressing concerns regarding noise impacts and proximity to residential area.

motions.title: Four two storey dwellings - West Leederville
motions.description: Application for four, two storey dwellings at Lots 20 and 21 (No. 387) Vincent Street West, corner Barrington Street, West Leederville. The site is triangular in shape with three attached dwellings facing Vincent Street West and a separate dwelling facing Barrington Street. The proposal has been assessed against Residential Design Codes and is not considered to satisfy relevant design principles for street setback, lot boundary setback, garage width, roof pitch, landscaping and vehicular access.

motions.title: Fees and Charges 2016-2017 adoption
motions.description: Development and Sustainability Services Schedule of Fees and Charges 2016-2017 covering planning, building, health and ranger services. Amendment moved to increase parking fee at 48 Cambridge Street from $15 to $20, which was lost.

motions.title: Refuse billboard relocation application
motions.description: Application to relocate existing billboard sign at Lot 2 (No. 138) Railway Parade, West Leederville. The sign is 42.411 square metres and contains third-party advertising. Proposal would relocate sign to face Railway Parade and railway line rather than Loftus Street intersection.

motions.title: Fencing front setback area - Lot 167 Hesperia Avenue approval
motions.description: Application for fencing within the front setback area as submitted by E Mangerf at Lot 167 (No. 34) Hesperia Avenue, City Beach. Originally recommended for refusal but amended plans received 21 April 2016 addressing design principles concerns.

motions.title: Support Design Review Panel introduction
motions.description: Support for introduction of independent Design Review Panel to provide advice on planning proposals and projects; adoption of draft Local Planning Policy 2.7 for advertising

motions.title: Local Planning Policy 5.2 Advertising Signs adoption
motions.description: Consideration of Local Planning Policy 5.2 Advertising Signs following a 31-day public advertising period from 4 March 2016 to 4 April 2016. Five submissions were received objecting to the policy on grounds of over-regulation and negative business impact. The modified policy seeks to clarify signage requirements, prohibit third-party advertising and large billboards, and exempt temporary and minor signs from approval.

motions.title: Receive report on alternatives to herbicide use
motions.description: Public information report on weed control methods used by the Town of Cambridge, including herbicide and non-herbicide alternatives across Parks Operations, Works Operations, Wembley Golf Course, and Sustainability areas.

motions.title: Underground Power Program - Four Revised Proposals
motions.description: Four revised proposals to be submitted for funding under Round 6 of the State Underground Power Program, each covering approximately 800 properties. Following an amendment, the motion addresses the handling of remaining lots and communication to property owners.

motions.title: Town Planning Scheme Amendment No. 31 - Modified Proposal
motions.description: Minister for Planning directed Council to modify and readvertise Scheme Amendment No. 31 with alternative density coding proposals for City Beach and Floreat Precincts, including R20 density bonus for corner lots, R30 split coding around local centres, and R40/R60 split coding along Cambridge Street.

motions.title: Scheme Amendment - Allow Councillor Grinceri to Participate (First Motion)
motions.description: Motion to allow Cr Grinceri to participate in discussion and vote on Scheme Amendment No. 31 matter on the basis that her financial interest is common to a significant number of electors or ratepayers.

motions.title: Scheme Amendment - Allow Councillor Grinceri to Participate (Second Motion)
motions.description: Motion to allow Cr Grinceri to participate in discussion (but not vote) on Scheme Amendment No. 31 matter on the basis that her financial interest is common to a significant number of electors or ratepayers.

motions.title: Town Planning Scheme Amendment 31 - Legal Action Report
motions.description: Report on ongoing legal action by Coast Ward Ratepayers Association challenging Council's decision to adopt Town Planning Scheme Amendment 31. Dismissal hearing was held in February 2016 with Justice Pritchard's decision pending. Costs to date total $132,666.

motions.title: Ocean Gardens (Inc) Board Composition
motions.description: Motion regarding governance of Ocean Gardens (Inc) retirement village, requesting the Town write to the CEO about board diversity, seek membership list, and have CEO review appointment criteria.

motions.title: Reimbursement of Legal Costs for Elected Members
motions.description: Motion to authorize reimbursement of legal costs up to $5,000 for elected members' independent legal advice regarding declaration of interest under s5.65 of the Local Government Act on complex scheme amendments.

motions.title: Prohibition of Gifts for CEO and Planning Staff
motions.description: Motion to prohibit gifts of entertainment for the Chief Executive Officer and planning staff from developers, architects and planners.

motions.title: Record Planning Staff Contact with Developers
motions.description: Motion requiring planning staff to record and report contact with developers, architects and planners for multiple dwelling developments and developments exceeding $2 million in value.

motions.title: Independent Legal Advice - Corner Contiguity Interest Declaration
motions.description: Motion to obtain independent legal advice regarding whether a councillor with corner contiguity to an affected property has a declarable interest under s5.65 of the Local Government Act.

motions.title: Policy - Taking of Leave by Chief Executive Officer
motions.description: Motion to develop a policy regarding the Chief Executive Officer's taking of leave and performance of duties while absent from Council offices.

motions.title: Confirmation of Minutes 22 March 2016 - Amendment to Q3(b)
motions.description: Motion to confirm minutes subject to amendment deleting reference to Cr Bradley in Question 3(b)

motions.title: Confirmation of Minutes 22 March 2016
motions.description: Motion to confirm minutes of 22 March 2016

motions.title: City Beach BioLINC Stage 1 - deferred
motions.description: Consideration of Cambridge Coastcare's request for matching funding of $150,000 to complement a Lotterywest grant of $150,000 for the City Beach BioLINC Stage 1 project. Council had previously committed to up to $152,000 funding in December 2015. The committee recommendation included a four-part amended motion requiring detailed design submission and approval before works commence.

motions.title: The Boulevard - Durston Road to Templetonia Crescent median extension
motions.description: Decision on design option for final median extension on The Boulevard between Durston Road and Templetonia Crescent. Two options were considered: Option 1 with central brown median islands ($90,000), and Option 2 with on-road cycle lanes ($190,000). Item was deferred from October 2015 to allow for development of the Town's Five Year Bike Plan.

motions.title: Roads to Recovery Grant 2015-16 additional project
motions.description: Endorsement of additional road resurfacing project for Essex Street (Ruislip Street to Grantham Street) using surplus Roads to Recovery Grant funding of $60,000 from three under-budget projects (Crofts Lane, Donegal Road, Launceston Avenue). Total surplus available is $141,657.

motions.title: Ruislip Street chicane removal between McKenzie and Daglish Streets
motions.description: Approval for removal of the last remaining chicane in the Wembley area traffic management program, to be replaced with speed plateaux. Works can be coordinated with upgrading of Waddington Lane. Funding of $18,000 from surplus completed project funds.

motions.title: Denton Street parking restrictions adoption
motions.description: Adoption of parking restrictions on Denton Street between Cambridge Street and Salvado Road. Parking survey distributed in March 2016 received 100% resident support for 2-hour parking with Residential Permit Parking Excepted on the west side. Estimated signage cost $420.

motions.title: Grantham Street/Harborne Street Black Spot project - Council decision
motions.description: Council decision on Grantham Street/Harborne Street Black Spot project. Main Roads WA reaffirmed Option C (dedicated right turn pockets) as preferred after Option B was rejected as ineffective and not addressing pedestrian safety. Preliminary cost estimates $1,100,000 exceeds $700,000 Federal grant. Council requests extension and reconsideration of Option B.

motions.title: Waste Minimisation Program Review - Amended Motion
motions.description: Council decision on waste minimisation initiatives including recycling collections, waste programs, and charity bins on public land.

motions.title: Waste Local Law 2016 - Commence law-making process
motions.description: Statutory review of local laws and commencement of the law-making process for the Town of Cambridge Waste Local Law 2016, replacing waste-related provisions in the Health Local Law.

motions.title: 30th Anniversary of the Quarry Amphitheatre
motions.description: Proposal to celebrate the 30th Anniversary of the Quarry Amphitheatre with activities including a free concert, historical exhibition, and documentary screening, with $20,000 budget allocation.

motions.title: 30th Anniversary of the Quarry Amphitheatre - Amended Motion
motions.description: Amended proposal to celebrate the 30th Anniversary with free concert, historical exhibition, and documentary screening, excluding cocktail sundowner.

motions.title: Quarry Amphitheatre - Amendment to Documentary Clause
motions.description: Amendment to change clause (iii) regarding the documentary from being screened to being produced only.

motions.title: 2016 Financial Assistance to Local Schools - Disbursement of Funds
motions.description: Approval of financial assistance grants to five local schools for various community benefit projects totaling $8,815, funded through a combination of budgeted amounts and Recreation Services budget savings.

motions.title: Alderbury Sportsground Needs Assessment
motions.description: Proposal to undertake a needs assessment and concept master plan for Alderbury Sportsground to guide future facility development for various sports clubs and community users.

motions.title: Alderbury Sportsground - Amendment for Two-Stage Process
motions.description: Amendment to clarify the two-stage process of needs assessment followed by concept master plan with conditional funding.

motions.title: Dodd Street Toilets - CCTV and Lighting Installation
motions.description: Proposal to install permanent lighting towers at Dodd Street cul-de-sac following successful trial, with community survey showing 94% support for the initiative.

motions.title: Dodd Street Toilets - Amendment to Remove CCTV
motions.description: Amendment to remove CCTV component and proceed with lighting towers only as primary crime prevention strategy.

motions.title: Perry Lakes Water Bodies - Funding for Options Study
motions.description: Proposal to fund a high level technical study into options for replenishing water levels in Perry Lakes, examining feasibility, costs, and regulatory issues of various approaches.

motions.title: City Beach Development Parking Expansion - Detail Design Approval
motions.description: Approval to undertake detail design of 120 bay expansion of Fred Burton Carpark with improved pedestrian crossings, following community consultation showing evenly divided feedback.

motions.title: City Beach Parking - Amendment to Remove Coastcare Consultation Requirement
motions.description: Amendment to delete the requirement for further consultation with Coastcare regarding carpark design modifications.

motions.title: Documents Sealed - April 2016
motions.description: Report advising Council of documents that have been affixed with the Common Seal of the Town of Cambridge. Three documents were sealed during March 2016, relating to heritage agreement caveat replacements and withdrawals for properties in City Beach and West Leederville.

motions.title: Ocean Gardens (Inc.) - Nomination for Director Appointment
motions.description: Report on the nomination of [private individual — name withheld] for appointment as a sixth Director of the Ocean Gardens (Inc.) Board. The Administration recommended approval, but the Committee voted against it (2/3). Council voted in favour of the appointment (6/3).

motions.title: Payment of Accounts - March 2016
motions.description: Report on payments of accounts made by the Town during March 2016 under the Local Government (Financial Management) Regulations 1996. Includes cheque payments totalling $293,867.44 and electronic fund transfers totalling $11,146,291.16.

motions.title: Investment Schedule - March 2016
motions.description: Report on the Council's investment portfolio performance for March 2016. Total investment of $27.3 million consisting of Municipal Funds of $11.7 million, Reserve Funds of $7.2 million, Endowment Lands Funds of $6.5 million and Trust Funds of $1.9 million. Weighted average interest rate of 2.96%.

motions.title: Monthly Financial Statements, Review and Variances - March 2016
motions.description: Report on the financial position for the period ended 31 March 2016 including analysis of operating revenue, operating expenses, capital works programs, and cash surplus with variances against budget.

motions.title: Tamala Park Regional Council Meetings - October 2015, December 2015, February 2016
motions.description: Report on items considered at Tamala Park Regional Council meetings held on 15 October 2015, 10 December 2015, and 18 February 2016. Covers project status, sales strategy, distributions, and infrastructure works for the Catalina development.

motions.title: City of Perth Surf Lifesaving Club - Financial Support Request
motions.description: Report on financial support request from the City of Perth Surf Lifesaving Club due to delays in handover of new premises. Council approved payment of balance grant and compensation for delay to be funded from liquidated damages.

motions.title: Public Parking Station - Lot 18 Railway Parade West Leederville
motions.description: Application for public parking station with 143 car parking bays and 14 motorcycle bays at Lot 18 No. 164 Railway Parade, West Leederville. Temporary use approved for two years pending future apartment development.

motions.title: Relocation of Existing Billboard Sign - Lot 2 Railway Parade West Leederville
motions.description: Application to reposition existing billboard sign from eastern side of building to above roofline facing south onto Railway Parade. Billboard contains third party advertising. Policy 5.2 has been amended to prohibit new billboard and electronic billboard signs.

motions.title: Approve change of use from shop to restaurant
motions.description: Application for change of use from shop (previously beautician) to restaurant at No. 442-444 Cambridge Street, Floreat. Located within Birkdale Street local centre. Proposed Italian restaurant with 20.6sqm seating area. Applicant to pay cash-in-lieu contribution of $15,000 for parking shortfall of 1 bay.

motions.title: Refuse home occupation motor vehicle air-conditioning servicing
motions.description: Application for home occupation at No. 205 Selby Street, Floreat. Proposal to operate motor vehicle air-conditioning servicing business from residential property. Involves specialist equipment and storage of refrigerant in liquefied form. Adjacent neighbour at No. 1 Evandale Street raised concerns about noise and amenity impacts.

motions.title: Refuse two storey dwelling application
motions.description: Application for two storey dwelling at Lot 7 (No. 93) Blencowe Street, West Leederville. Proposal includes double garage with nil side setback adjacent to street rather than access from adjoining right-of-way (Porter Lane). Upper floor roofed balcony setback only 4 metres from street. Roof pitch 26 degrees rather than required 30-40 degrees.

motions.title: Approve amended plan for loft space in two storey dwelling
motions.description: Application for amended plan to include loft space in two storey dwelling at No. 48 Hesperia Avenue, City Beach. Originally approved dwelling is currently under construction. Amended plans extend roof ridge to rear to create loft space. Minor wall height variation at rear (6.65m vs 6.5m deemed-to-comply). Four objections received from neighbouring properties during consultation.

motions.title: Approve additions and alterations including second storey and double carport
motions.description: Application for additions and alterations to original brick and tile bungalow at No. 59 Daglish Street, Wembley. Proposes double carport adjacent to street, bike store on south side, and two storey addition at rear replacing single storey addition. One objection received from adjoining property to south regarding wall height, site works and visual privacy.

motions.title: Approve fencing in front setback area
motions.description: Application for fencing within front setback area at No. 16 Alyth Road, Floreat. Proposes visually permeable fencing along southern end of front boundary and combination of visually permeable and solid fencing along southern side boundary. First 2.0 metres visually permeable, remainder solid. Condition requires extension of visually permeable fencing to 6.0 metres to enhance streetscape.

motions.title: State Administrative Tribunal reconsideration - 10 dwellings Connaught Street West Leederville
motions.description: SAT reconsideration of Council's refusal of amended plans for ten multiple dwellings at Lot 501 (No. 31) Connaught Street, West Leederville. Amended plans dated 1 April 2016 address previous reasons for refusal regarding building height, site works, overshadowing and ground level fill.

motions.title: Draft Perth and Peel Green Growth Plan for 3.5 Million submission
motions.description: Council submission on the Draft Perth and Peel Green Growth Plan for 3.5 Million to Department of Premier and Cabinet. Plan addresses environmental and conservation matters to facilitate implementation of draft Perth and Peel @ 3.5 million. Submission period closes 13 May 2016.

motions.title: Local Planning Strategy Project Plan endorsement
motions.description: Endorsement of the Local Planning Strategy Project Plan to guide the preparation of a Local Planning Strategy in accordance with Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015. Project plan outlines objectives, key steps, community engagement, project management and milestones.

The Town recorded the fourth highest number of local government admissions to NAR in 2015 with 124 admissions. NAR operates at approximately $15,000/month and is seeking funding support. The City of Swan contributes $15,000-$25,000/year and City of Bayswater contributes $11,000/year.

The policy was due for biennial review in April 2014. Changes align street numbering for subdivided and strata titled properties with the Australian Standard and allow for allocation of street numbers for ancillary dwellings.

motions.description: Application for a two storey dwelling at Lot 889 (No. 20C) Jukes Way, Wembley by [private individual — name withheld] and [private individual — name withheld]. motions.description: Application for street fencing, a vehicle crossover and a pergola to an upper floor balcony at Lot 1 (No. 20) Joseph Street, corner Woolwich Street, West Leederville. The application sought to vary Condition 2 of the previous planning approval (DV14.90) which restricted street fencing. Committee members expressed concern about the lack of visual truncation on the secondary street fence.

motions.title: Rear boundary wall abutting Challenger Park, City Beach
motions.description: Application for a rear boundary wall at Lot 10 (No. 48) Branksome Gardens, City Beach. The proposal comprised a solid limestone wall abutting parkland with a maximum height of 2.08 metres, which did not satisfy the design principles for passive surveillance of the parkland. Mayor Withers disclosed an impartiality interest before consideration.

motions.title: Perth and Peel @ 3.5 Million and Central Sub-regional Planning Framework
motions.description: Consideration of the Western Australian Planning Commission's draft Perth and Peel @ 3.5 million strategy and Central Sub-Regional Planning Framework, which provides guidance on land use and infrastructure over 30-40 years. The Town of Cambridge is located within the Central Sub-region with a revised housing target of 6,900 dwellings by 2050. The submission period to the WAPC closes 31 July 2015.

motions.title: Town Planning Policy 5.1 - Revised Parking Policy for Final Adoption
motions.description: Council adopted a revised Policy 5.1 for commercial parking, updating car parking ratio and cash-in-lieu provisions. The Town reassessed the cash-in-lieu requirement as current rates were underestimated. The draft policy was advertised and received two submissions: one letter of no objection and one letter of support. Key changes include increased cash-in-lieu rates to $15,000 per bay, introduction of parking ratios for Health Studio and Medical Centre uses, and lighting requirements for car parking areas.

motions.title: Lot 181 Cambridge Street West Leederville - Proposed Scheme Amendment Hospital
motions.description: Amendment to introduce additional use 'hospital (special purposes)' for Abbottsford Private Hospital. The hospital has operated since 2011 and sought Scheme Amendment to support existing and future use. Through advertising, the Town received one letter of support, one letter of conditional support and three letters of objection from nearby neighbours. The additional use does not alter existing residential zoning and is supported as the current business has continued to operate and any future proposal will be subject to additional development standards.

motions.title: Lot 12 Connolly Street Wembley - Two x Three Storey Grouped Dwellings SAT Reconsideration
motions.description: State Administrative Tribunal reconsideration of Council's decision of 24 March 2015 to refuse planning approval for two x three storey grouped dwellings. Following mediation, amended plans were submitted addressing height, setbacks, landscaping, vehicle access, and visual dominance issues. The applicant has made numerous amendments including reducing building height by 502mm, modifying driveway design to single crossover, reducing fill, and providing additional landscaping.

motions.title: Lot 501 Marlow Street Wembley - Two Storey Dwelling SAT Reconsideration
motions.description: State Administrative Tribunal reconsideration of Council's decision to refuse a two storey dwelling application on 28 April 2015. Following mediation, amended plans were submitted showing the garage modified to a guest room with a large window facing the street, and a double carport in the front setback. The amended plans satisfy the Town's Streetscape requirements with street surveillance provided and no double garage.

motions.title: Lot 462 St Leonards Avenue West Leederville - Two Storey Dwelling SAT Reconsideration
motions.description: State Administrative Tribunal reconsideration of Council's decision of 28 April 2015 to refuse a two storey dwelling application. Following a Directions Hearing on 3 June 2015, amended plans were submitted increasing setback from front boundary, addressing visual privacy issues, and providing parking from rear ROW. The amended plans increase the primary street setback to St Leonards Avenue, modify upper storey windows to address privacy concerns, and provide parking access via rear right of way.

The policy was advertised between 27 November and 22 December 2014 with 15 submissions received. The revised policy limits building heights in the Residential Interface Node to four storeys with buildings presenting as two storeys to adjoining residential properties.

The budget incorporates a 5.5% general rate increase based on estimated general increase in net cost of services and increased rate funding for asset renewal. General rates levied at 6.8103 cents per dollar on GRV properties and 0.2024 cents per dollar on UV properties with minimum rate of $836. Waste service charges imposed on rateable properties for domestic and commercial waste bins, recycling services, and optional green waste service. Amendment moved to include Harrogate Street Parking Embayments ($25,000) in roadworks capital projects and to incorporate separate development contribution reserve consistent with 26 June 2012 decision (CR12.94).

motions.description: Approval of project delivery and financial arrangements for the Wembley Sports Park including the State Netball Centre and Matthews Netball Works, noting the Minister for Sport and Recreation's letter dated 21 November 2011, approving delivery arrangements for PNA building and court reconfiguration works funded by a State Government Financial Assistance Agreement grant of $7.48 million (excl GST), Town-funded signalised intersection at Selby Street estimated at $500,000 (excl GST), car parks and roads on the east of the Wembley Sports Park, design fee deduction of $315,000 (excl GST), infrastructure contribution deduction of $134,000 (excl GST), shared cost of east/west access road and roundabout with Town contribution capped at $430,000 (excl GST), resulting in $6,601,000 payable by State Government to the Town and $850,000 savings to the State Government. motions.title: Cambridge Library entertainment DVD rental charges
motions.description: Decision on whether to introduce charges for hiring entertainment DVDs from Cambridge Library. Report assessed copyright restrictions, potential markets, library service directions, and financial implications. Copyright Act 1968 differentiates between lending and renting; current stock carries warning that hiring is prohibited. Research identified two Australian libraries (Wyndham and Geelong) which have ceased charging for DVD hire.

motions.title: Cambridge Library overdue loan fines introduction
motions.description: Proposal to introduce fines for overdue library loans at Cambridge Library effective 1 July 2010. Report notes that Western Australian libraries have historically not been strong advocates of fines, but trend to introduce overdue fines has emerged. Library Board identified eleven library systems currently charging penalties. Proposed fee structure: 20 cents per item per day commencing first day after due date, with $5.00 maximum charge per item.

Main concerns from objectors related to proposed development concept plan including overshadowing, overlooking, visual impact, and traffic/parking issues.

During committee discussion, Members expressed concern about the extent of parking in the front setback area in light of traffic congestion in McCourt Street.

motions.title: Single storey dwelling at Lot 77 St Columbas Avenue, Wembley

The dwelling consists of a double garage to the front with parapet wall on the south-western boundary, and a storeroom parapet wall to the rear on the south-western boundary abutting the Right-of-Way. Neighbouring property owner objected to the proposal.

motions.title: Two grouped dwellings at Lot 10 St Leonards Avenue, West Leederville

Applicant Parm Tjhung Designs Pty Ltd. Neighbour objections to side setbacks and wall height were received; amended plans addressing setback concerns were submitted. Pool patio roof height reduction required as a condition.

motions.title: Additions to single dwelling at Glengariff Drive Floreat

Additions include outdoor living area with parapet wall on western boundary, conversion of garage to games room with crossover removal, double carport with Ulster Road access, and verge tree removal. One objection received regarding noise from entertaining area near neighbour's bedroom.

motions.title: Two storey grouped dwelling at Daglish Street Wembley

Proposal utilizes Wembley Corner Lot policy allowing two dwellings on R20 zoned corner lots under R30 density standards. Ground floor includes double garage, living areas and bedroom; upper floor includes four bedrooms and family/theatre/study room. Neighbour objection received regarding setbacks and building scale; amended plans submitted addressing side setback and visual privacy concerns.

motions.title: Loft and spa addition and alterations at Ruislip Street West Leederville
motions.description: Application for loft and spa addition and alterations to existing dwelling at Lot 1 (No. 20) Ruislip Street, West Leederville. Applicant Philip McAllister Architect Pty Ltd. Proposal includes loft area in existing roof with two bedrooms, bathroom and retreat; alterations to existing basement to create gym; outdoor spa with fence and decking. Wall height variations assessed under performance criteria. Neighbour objections received regarding privacy and boundary issues; amended plans with fixed obscure glass windows to west and east facing loft windows submitted.

motions.description: Application for additions and alterations including second storey addition to existing single storey dwelling at Lot 729 (No. 19) Goonang Road, corner Gunee Road, City Beach. Applicant Celebration Nominees trading as Dale Alcock Home Improvement. Proposal includes new ensuite, WIR and laundry on ground floor on south-eastern side adjacent to Gunee Road; new upper floor with main bedroom, retreat, ensuite, walk-in-robe and balconies above ground floor closest to corner. Secondary street setback and building height variations assessed. Neighbour objections addressed; neighbours of some adjacent properties provided written consent.

motions.title: SAT direction to review shed Building Approval Certificate application
motions.description: Application for Building Approval Certificate for unauthorised shed at Lot 809 (No. 1) Turriff Road, Floreat. Applicant [private individual — name withheld]. At State Administrative Tribunal direction, Council reconsidered application for shed existing since 2006 constructed without approval. Shed measuring 10.259m long by 4.23m wide, 2.1m high, located on southern boundary with nil setback (1.5m required). Building Code of Australia compliance assessment identified multiple breaches in structural fixing and roofing specifications. Neighbour submission received objecting to eyesore appearance affecting area amenity and property values.

Council consideration required for front fence piers variation.

Landing constructed of limestone blocks, 6m x 4.1m with maximum height 0.7m, attached to rear of dwelling. Neighbouring property to west objected on privacy grounds citing overlooking to courtyard, dining room and bedrooms. Proposal assessed against R Codes performance criteria for visual privacy with consideration of screening provided by existing vegetation, shed and fence.

motions.title: Fencing in street setback Lot 802 Salvado Road Floreat

Proposed treated pine picket fence 1.2m high along Lissadell Street (primary); along Salvado Road (secondary) same fence sits on limestone retaining wall ranging 100-500mm, increasing total height to 1.7m. Fence exceeds permeability provisions of RDGs. Solid gate proposed on eastern boundary.

motions.title: Proposed front fence Lot 418 Adina Road City Beach

Proposed combination of permeable fencing with infill panels and solid fencing to maximum 2.10m height. Designed to retain two large native eucalypt trees. Fence encloses front setback area providing privacy and screening from vehicle headlight glare and traffic noise.

motions.title: Proposed fencing Lot 4 Boronia Crescent City Beach

Southern boundary includes 0.5m retaining wall with 1.8m wall above. Three piers exceed maximum width. Neighbours consulted.

motions.title: Retrospective approval illegally constructed loft Lot 174 Tilton Terrace City Beach

Loft wall height 8.3m exceeds prescribed 6.5m. Visual privacy issues with overlooking to adjoining properties. Neighbours objected on grounds of illegal construction, height, privacy, and questioning Council's authority to grant retrospective approval.

Motion includes funding advising PIAF of Council's valuing of their performances and noise restrictions report requirement.

motions.title: Wembley Traffic Management – Referendum by WA Electoral Commission

motions.title: West Coast Highway – Access to Floreat Beach
motions.description: That Council immediately seeks a meeting with Main Roads WA in order to request them to reallocate funds, as a priority, in order to resolve the dangerous situation regarding vehicle access from the West Coast Highway to Floreat Beach.

motions.title: TravelSmart Individualised Marketing

motions.title: Brompton Road/Kilpa Court Intersection – Directional Sign

motions.title: Construction Works – Four capital works projects

motions.title: Bulk Waste Verge Collection Service
motions.description: Consideration of tenders for bulk waste verge collection service. Five tenders were received. The administration recommended D&M Waste (an alternative proposal with lower cost), but the committee preferred to continue with the existing contractor Alvito to maintain current service.

motions.title: WA Football Commission Additional Night Games Opposition

motions.title: Town Planning Scheme Amendment - Subdivision Policy

motions.title: Budget for the Year Ended 30 June 2002
motions.description: Adoption of 2001/2002 Budget with 9.9% gross rental rate increase, minimum rate increase from $442 to $486, and capital works increase of $533,000. Major items include $244,000 additional waste management costs and rates levied.

motions.title: Leave of Absence for Councillor Smith

motions.description: Application for two storey dwelling with variations to setback, side setbacks, rear setback and roof pitch requirements at Lot 4 Bernard Street, West Leederville, submitted by Riverstone Constructions.

motions.description: Application for upper level addition and portico at Lot 747 (No. 61) Peebles Road, Floreat, seeking variation to building height provisions of Residential Design Guidelines.

motions.description: Application for alterations and additions including rear addition, front addition with swimming pool and additional level at Lot 390 (No. 23) Catesby Street, City Beach, seeking variations to multiple requirements.

motions.description: Application for construction of carport with front setback variation at Lot 204 (No. 1) Penryn Avenue, corner Callington Street, City Beach.

motions.description: Application for construction of landscaping feature fence with height variation at Lot 106 (No. 8) Poolya Road, City Beach.
